item.content:encoded:
While I don't find this SCP particularly horrifying, I did feel it was well-written and intriguing, and it definitely appealed to me as a gamer. The omission of an Agility-focused subject from the test log does seem rather odd, though. I can't think of a good reason why the Foundation would investigate 5 avenues of study and neglect the 6th.

Also, random question: was there a particular reason you chose to have all 5 test subjects be male? I generally tend to feel that when writing about groups of people, the group should be gender-balanced by default, unless there's a compelling reason to weight it towards one gender or the other. Just curious what your thoughts were.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I think doesn't necessarily mean that the Foundation is inherently "wise" in all it does, or even in most of what it does, just that Cleric ended up agreeing with it in the end. Someone with a different background or different moral convictions might have come to the opposite conclusion, that what the Foundation is doing is wrong, and that the end does not justify the means. It's also not made clear precisely how much he was actually told; he can only make his judgement based on what he knows, and the Foundation is very good at convincing themselves that they're in the right.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I was prepared to hate this as soon as I realized the concept. But have come around to neutral because you executed the premise well.

I think it mainly suffers from being too long in parts and not having enough impact. Length is just a matter of tweaking, the first paragraph of containment could be cut totally, for example.

Adding impact, by which I mean horror/squick-ness, is less easy; and I'm not sure I have any useful suggestions. Maybe an un-rounded character becomes physcially distorted in painful and interesting ways. Over-leveling srength too quickly causes muscles to balloon unsustainably and rupture the skin, sort of thing. It's an idea you touch on when the Berserker tries to escape, the body can't support the strength he has. Just more graphic. Of course, that might spoil the story of the test group, which is the best part of this article, so please take my suggestions lightly.

I don't hate it. You did put a lot of thought into this, but it feels like you have to go through too much to get too little in return. There's no real twist, apart from the Cleric becoming cooperative due to increased wisdom, which is actually my least favorite part of the entire piece because it labels the Foundation's activities as "wise" rather than ambiguous. Bard's charisma feels like a cop out because he has a magical smile instead of being better at understanding and manipulating people.

A better twist would have been the super intelligent warlock using his new stats to screw everyone else and escape not by getting out of the Foundation but tricking everyone into believing that he is actually one of the head researchers who was working within the game and falsifying necessary records to support that.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Can't help feeling that it's a SCP of the "too useful" variety. There'd be no downside in using this for increasing the abilities of the Foundation's agents, for example.

Besides, there's no real hook here; nothing particularly scary, weird or interesting, and the addendums feel a lot like padding. Also, the idea of the Foundation not only sparing a D-class that was contaminated by an SCP, but actually letting him near other SCP objects, even ones classified as Safe (a label that, contrary to popular belief, doesn't indicate that the object isn't dangerous), is ludicrous to say the least.

The tone is decent, though.
